Save a plot to a file sized to fit it

Source: R/plot_size.R
save_plot.Rd

Saves a ggplot or patchwork to PDF (vector), PNG or any format ggsave supports.

For plots whose panels have a fixed size (all plots of this package, or any ggplot with panel_size_theme), the width and height of the file are computed from the panels, strips, legends and margins, so that nothing is cropped and no white space is added. They are measured on the same kind of device the file is written with, so that font metrics match. Patchworks of such plots, including nested ones, keep the size of every panel.

Plots without fixed panel sizes are saved at `width` by `height` inches, as with ggsave().

A legend from extract_legend is saved on its own, sized to fit, with a small margin.

PDFs are written with cairo_pdf when R has cairo support (capabilities("cairo")): fonts are embedded, Unicode text is drawn, and a hyphen stays a hyphen (base pdf() draws "-" with the wider minus glyph). The default font family is set to the one the PNG device (ragg) uses, so PDF and PNG files of a plot match; a family named explicitly ("sans", "Arial", ...) is passed on as it is. Without cairo, or when `device` is given, ggsave()'s device is used.

Usage

save_plot(
  plot,
  filename,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  dpi = 1000,
  bg = NULL,
  minus = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot or patchwork object, or a legend from extract_legend

filename

File to save to; the format is inferred from the extension (".pdf", ".png", ".svg", ".tiff", ...)

width, height

Size of the file in inches, used only for plots without fixed panel sizes, for which they are required. Default is NULL

dpi

Resolution of raster formats, default is 1000

bg

Background colour. If NULL (default), taken from the plot. A transparent background is kept in PDF, PNG, TIFF and SVG; formats without transparency (JPEG, BMP) get a white one instead

minus

If TRUE (default), negative numbers in the labels of continuous scales (axes, colour bars) are written with a true minus sign (U+2212) rather than a hyphen. Text typed in titles or labels is not changed. Applies to PDFs written with cairo and to raster files written with ragg, the devices that can draw the minus sign

...

Additional arguments passed to ggsave

Value

The width and height of the saved file in inches, invisibly

See also

panel_size_theme, export_source_data, extract_legend

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point() +
    theme_bioToolkit() + panel_size_theme(2.5, 2)
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
save_plot(p, f)
